name: Sly Cooper (ProjectCane)

original.title: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus

assets.needs: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus NTSC-U PS2 disc image (.iso, SCUS-97198). The app checks SYSTEM.CNF and SCUS_971.98 in the ISO root, then extracts levels, audio and cutscenes on the device (about 4 GB free needed).
assets.location: Picked once with Android's document picker (ImportActivity: 'Select PS2 ISO and extract'); extracted data goes to /sdcard/Android/data/org.projectcane.cane/files (Worlds/, Cutscenes/, SecondScreen/). The ISO itself is not read again after extraction.
assets.notes: Extracted data takes about 2.8 GB. After extraction the game boots to the title screen.

settings.in_app_menu: In-game Settings menu (Video..., keyboard/controller configuration, 'Reset Video Settings'). Save backup/restore and the debug-log export are a separate Android screen (SavesActivity) reached from the game.
settings.summary: Game and video settings live in system_settings.dat, a binary file with the magic PCANESYS (SavesActivity backs it up with the saves), so there is no text file to edit and no adapter. Android SharedPreferences 'cane' hold two dual-screen keys: secondScreen (bool, default true: show episode art / cutscene frames on the Thor's bottom screen) and secondScreenArt (int 0-9, art style, cycled in game). The app also picks the display refresh rate from the panel's supported modes (CaneActivity.supportedRefreshRates). Other native files named in libmain.so: touch_settings.cfg, gui_proportions.cfg, imgui.ini, content_settings.json.

controls: SDL2 game controller input plus a touch overlay (touch_settings.cfg). Keyboard and controller remapping screens exist in the game's menu (strings 'Configuration de la manette', 'Keyboard'). Not tested on the Thor.
display: Game on the top screen. On a device with a second presentation display (the Thor's bottom screen) it starts SecondScreenActivity there, showing episode art and cutscene frames; toggled with the secondScreen pref. Native GPU renderer needs vertex SSBOs (it shows an error naming SSBO limits on weak GPUs); the Adreno 740 should pass but this is not checked.
saves: /sdcard/Android/data/org.projectcane.cane/files/Saves/slot1.sav ... slot9.sav (magic PCANESAV) plus system_settings.dat. Uninstalling the app deletes them; the in-app 'Back up saves to a file' writes a zip.
notes: The Android wrapper's source could not be identified. Upstream ProjectCane (theclub654) publishes Windows/Linux builds only (release 'decompilation', 2026-10-21). Tried: GitHub code search for 'org.projectcane.cane' and 'CaneActivity' (no hits), repo search 'ProjectCane' (theclub654/ProjectCane, FridiNaTor1/ProjectCane-old, sinzcyro/ProjectCane, Raihwy3/ThieviusCTR 3DS port, baconspaceman/ProjectCane-AP), FridiNaTor1/SafeHouse (its Android app is org.safehouse.android, a different package), web search, and strings in the APK (no URL, no update checker; version-control-info says NO_SUPPORTED_VCS_FOUND). APK SHA-256 5604f4d60d364b93a9f4acc79aea15fe0449db0050538b872dfe56ac571ec553. Package also ships FFmpeg (libavcodec/libavformat) for the m2v cutscenes and libbrxrebuild.so, which rebuilds the extracted levels.

APK decompiled with jadx: ISO checks, extraction paths, Saves dir, PCANESYS/PCANESAV magics, 'cane' prefs keys, second-screen behaviour. Web/GitHub: upstream repo only. Not checked: any in-game setting, controls or performance.
